summary: Naturalist and bird painter John James Audubon, namesake of the Audubon Society, bought and sold enslaved people in Kentucky, faked a bird species to raise funds, and robbed Indigenous graves for skulls supplied to race scientist Samuel Morton.

evidence.note: born in Saint-Domingue (modern Haiti) to a French slave-trading captain
raised in Nantes, France before being sent to Pennsylvania
early bird-banding experiment on the family farm in Pennsylvania
works as a slave dealer and keeps enslaved people in Kentucky households
invents the nonexistent Bird of Washington to raise money in Europe
Runaway tale in Ornithological Biography returning a fugitive family to slavery
Morton as patron; craniometry and the roots of scientific racism
1843 Missouri trip: takes skulls from Assiniboine burials after smallpox
Morton skulls held by Penn Museum, slow NAGPRA repatriation to the present
Audubon Society's 2020 reckoning with his record after a Central Park incident
